subject.title: feat(memory): expose QMD rerank candidate limit

question: Should OpenClaw expose QMD’s reranker candidate limit as a supported user-facing `memory.qmd` configuration control, rather than keeping query-mode performance tuning limited to the existing mode, rerank, and timeout controls?
rationale: This is a new persisted configuration and operator-facing performance contract; implementation quality alone cannot establish whether the additional public knob fits the project’s high bar for config surface growth.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow opt-in control
options.body: Accept the field only with an explicit QMD capability/version contract and real OpenClaw proof for both direct and mcporter query paths.

options.title: Keep the current controls
options.body: Decline the additional setting and direct operators to the existing search-mode, rerank, and timeout choices.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow opt-in control
recommendation.body: Accept the field only with an explicit QMD capability/version contract and real OpenClaw proof for both direct and mcporter query paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on the QMD recall-mode boundary makes this person the strongest available routing candidate for the configuration-direction decision.
